title: Insights
intro: Insights are Pega's reporting building blocks in Constellation: queries built in Explore Data and saved as tables or charts that can be shared and placed on dashboards, portal landing pages and Full Page case views. Expect questions about where an Insight can and cannot go, simple value charts, and common troubleshooting fixes.

objectives.objective: Describe the benefits of using Insights
summary: An **Insight** is a rule that turns a data query into a table or chart. Because it is a saved rule rather than a one-off query, it can be shared with other users and reused in several places, such as dashboards, portal landing pages and case pages. Insights come in table-based and chart-based forms.

Insights are built in the Explore Data landing page, which is the preferred reporting experience for Constellation applications. Pega GenAI Autopilot can also help create an Insight from a natural-language request.
keyFacts: Insight = a rule that turns a query into a table or chart.
Insights are shareable and reusable across dashboards, portal landing pages and Full Page case views.
Two forms: table-based and chart-based.
Explore Data is the preferred place to build them for Constellation.
Autopilot can create an Insight from natural language.
examTraps: An Insight is a saved rule, not a temporary query that disappears after the session.
Insights are a Constellation-oriented feature; Traditional UI apps need extra enablement (see Explore Data).

objectives.objective: Use the Explore Data landing page to create Insights
summary: The **Explore Data** landing page lets users query, sort, filter and group application data and then save the result as an Insight. It is the preferred option for Constellation applications. Traditional UI applications must enable Constellation UI for landing pages before they can use it. Object names shown in Explore Data come from each class's short description.

A **simple value chart** displays a single headline number. It is produced when only Measures fields are used (no grouping dimensions). Layouts are Highlight, Highlight + summary, and Custom highlight + summary, and conditional formatting can color the value based on thresholds.
keyFacts: Explore Data supports query, sort, filter and group, then save as Insight.
Traditional UI apps must enable Constellation UI for landing pages to use Explore Data.
Object names in Explore Data come from the class short description.
Simple value chart appears when only Measures fields are selected.
Simple value layouts: Highlight; Highlight + summary; Custom highlight + summary.
Simple value charts support conditional formatting.

rows: A customized highlight plus a summary

examTraps: Adding a grouping/dimension field means it is no longer a simple value chart; only measures qualify.
Explore Data is not automatically available to Traditional UI apps.
Odd object names in Explore Data are fixed through the class short description, not the Insight.

objectives.objective: Describe the relationship between Insights, Dashboards, the Dashboards landing page, Portal landing pages, and Full Page Case Views
summary: Insights can be placed in three kinds of location. On a **Full Page case view**, an Insight can only be added as a tab, not directly inside a View. On **portal landing pages**, public Insights can be added to a region. On **dashboards**, Insights are arranged in a template; dashboards have private, shared (users with access, either all users or your access group) or public visibility, and a promoted filter applies across all Insights on the dashboard.

The **Dashboards landing page** is available by default in App Studio and in work portals and is not configured through portal authoring; a default Work metrics dashboard is provided. Dashboards are landing pages made of widgets that summarize KPIs per persona, built from a template with regions (for example a two-column template with Region A and Region B). New dashboards are private by default, and a copy keeps the source dashboard's visibility. Out-of-the-box portal landing pages include Dashboard, Home, Explore Data, My Work and Self-service Main page.
keyFacts: Full Page case view: Insights only as tabs, never directly inside a View.
Portal landing pages: only public Insights can be added to a region.
Dashboard visibility: private (default for new), shared, public.
A copied dashboard keeps the source's visibility.
A promoted filter applies to every Insight on a dashboard.
Dashboards landing page is available by default in App Studio and work portals; not set up through portal authoring.
A default Work metrics dashboard exists.
Explore Data and Dashboard are among the out-of-the-box portal landing pages.

rows: Visibility private/shared/public; promoted filter spans all Insights
Available by default in App Studio and work portals

examTraps: Insights cannot be embedded in a partial or form View; use a tab on the Full Page case view.
A private Insight cannot be placed on a portal landing page.
New dashboards default to private, not public.
Do not look for the Dashboards landing page in portal authoring.

summary: Common Insights problems have specific fixes. Repeated login prompts are addressed by adjusting the access token lifetime. Unwanted number separators in table columns are fixed by modifying the UI controls. Strange object names in Explore Data come from class short descriptions. A missing column usually means the backing property must be optimized for reporting (in the parent classes as well as the specific class) or marked as a relevant record.

Stale display issues can come from the browser cache: close pages, use an incognito window or clear session storage. If the Constellation portal or Explore Data fails to load, verify the application settings, alias and authentication types, and the OAuth 2.0 Client Registration rule.
keyFacts: Repeated login prompts: adjust the access token lifetime.
Number separators in tables: modify the UI controls.
Explore Data object names: class short description.
Missing column: optimize the property for reporting in parent classes and the specific class, or mark it relevant.
Browser cache issues: close pages, use incognito, clear session storage.
Portal/Explore Data load failures: check application settings, alias, authentication types and the OAuth 2.0 Client Registration rule.
examTraps: Optimizing a property only in the specific class may not be enough; parent classes matter too.
Login prompts are a token lifetime issue, not an access role issue.
Load failures point to app settings/auth/OAuth client registration, not to the Insight definition.

questions.stem: Every Monday a regional manager rebuilds the same filtered, grouped list of overdue claims and emails screenshots to colleagues. What removes this repeated work?
options: Save the Explore Data query as an Insight and share it.
Ask a developer to add the list to the claim's Create Form View.
Mark the claim properties as relevant records.
Turn the list into a Decision table that colleagues can open.
questions.explanation: Insights are rules that turn Explore Data queries into tables or charts that can be saved and shared, so the manager builds the list once and colleagues open it directly. A Create Form View collects input when a case is created and does not present a reusable query. Marking properties as relevant records makes them available in App Studio but does not save the query. A Decision table returns results from conditions and is not a reporting tool.

questions.stem: A business lead is evaluating Insights for her operations team. Which two statements are correct? (Choose Two)
options: Insights are rules that turn queries into tables or charts.
Insights can be shared with other users.
Insights can only be charts, so tables must stay in Explore Data.
Insights can be embedded directly in any Form View.
questions.explanation: Insights are rules that turn queries into visualizations, and they can be shared. Both table-based and chart-based Insights exist, so tables are not limited to Explore Data. On a case, Insights are placed in tabs of the Full Page View, not directly inside a View such as a Form View.

questions.stem: A company has an older application built with Traditional UI. Business users want to use Explore Data to build their own Insights. What must happen first?
options: Enable Constellation UI for landing pages in the application.
Rebuild every Case Type as a Constellation Case Type.
Create a Report Definition for each Insight in Dev Studio.
Add the Explore Data page to the portal through portal authoring.
questions.explanation: Explore Data is the preferred approach for Constellation. Traditional UI applications must enable Constellation UI for landing pages before they can use it. Rebuilding every Case Type goes far beyond what is needed. Insights are created from Explore Data queries, not one Report Definition at a time. Adding a page through portal authoring does not meet the Constellation landing page requirement.

questions.stem: In Explore Data, an analyst wants a tile that shows the total number of open claims as one large number. She selects the Count measure and also adds Region as a column, but the simple value chart is not offered. Why?
options: A simple value chart needs Measures fields only, so Region must be removed.
The Count measure is not supported, so she must switch to Sum.
Simple value charts are available only after the Insight is added to a Dashboard.
Conditional formatting must be turned on before simple value charts appear.
questions.explanation: The Simple Value visualization is available only when the query contains just Measures fields. Adding a grouping column such as Region removes the option. Count is a valid measure. Simple value charts are built in Explore Data and do not have to be placed on a Dashboard first. Conditional formatting is an optional feature of a simple value chart, not a condition for offering one.

questions.stem: A dashboard designer wants a simple value chart that shows the open-claims count as a large number with a supporting summary. Which two layouts provide this? (Choose Two)
options: Highlight + summary
Custom highlight + summary
Highlight
Summary + trend line
questions.explanation: The simple value chart has three layouts: Highlight, Highlight + summary, and Custom highlight + summary. Only the two that include a summary meet the requirement. Highlight on its own is a real layout but has no summary. Summary + trend line is not a layout offered for simple value charts.

questions.stem: Case workers want to see an Insight of related open orders while they work on an order case. Where should the developer add it?
options: To a tab of the order Case Type's Full Page View
Inside the order's Details Partial View
Inside the Create Form View for the order
To the Pulse view in the summary panel
questions.explanation: On a case, Insights can be placed only in tabs of the Full Page Case View. They cannot be added directly inside a View, so the Details Partial View and the Create Form View are both wrong. Pulse in the summary panel is for posting and replying to messages in the context of the case, and it does not host Insights.

questions.stem: A team lead is setting up Dashboards for her team. Which two statements are correct? (Choose Two)
options: A new Dashboard is private by default.
A promoted filter applies to every Insight on the Dashboard.
A copied Dashboard is always private, whatever the visibility of the source.
The Dashboards landing page must be added to each Work Portal through portal authoring.
questions.explanation: New Dashboards are private by default and can be shared with an Access Group or made public. A promoted filter applies across all Insights on the Dashboard. A copy keeps the visibility of its source Dashboard, so it is not always private. The Dashboards landing page is available by default in App Studio and in Work Portals, and it is not configured through portal authoring.

questions.stem: A developer edits a portal landing page and wants to add an Insight she shared with her Access Group yesterday. It does not appear in the list for the region, but other colleagues' Insights do. What is the most likely reason?
options: Portal landing pages accept only public Insights, and hers is shared with an Access Group only.
The Insight must be placed on a Dashboard before it can be added to a landing page.
Landing page regions accept only table-based Insights.
The Insight must first be added to a tab of a Full Page View.
questions.explanation: Portal landing page regions take public Insights only. Sharing an Insight with an Access Group is a real visibility level, but it is not enough for a landing page. An Insight does not need to be placed on a Dashboard or in a Full Page View tab first. Both table-based and chart-based Insights exist, and the region does not limit them by type.

questions.stem: A new application team is planning where users will see Insights. Which two statements are correct? (Choose Two)
options: Public Insights can be added to a region on a portal landing page.
The Dashboards landing page, with a default Work metrics Dashboard, is available in Work Portals by default.
An Insight can be embedded directly in a case's Partial View.
A Dashboard is made of Insights placed straight onto the page, without templates or regions.
questions.explanation: Public Insights can be placed in a region of a portal landing page. The Dashboards landing page is available by default in App Studio and in Work Portals, and it includes a default Work metrics Dashboard. On a case, Insights appear only in tabs of the Full Page View, not directly inside a View such as a Partial View. Dashboards are built from a template divided into regions that hold widgets, such as the two-column Work metrics layout.

questions.stem: A developer adds the property RepairCost to a claim Case Type, but it does not appear as a column option in Explore Data. Which action is most likely to fix this?
options: Optimize the property for reporting in the claim class and in its parent classes.
Optimize the property for reporting only in the specific claim class.
Clear the browser session storage and reopen Explore Data.
Change the claim class's short description.
questions.explanation: When a column is missing, optimize its backing property for reporting in both the parent classes and the specific class, or mark the property as a relevant record. Optimizing it only in the specific class is incomplete. Clearing session storage fixes cached page problems, not a missing property. The class short description sets the object name shown in Explore Data, not which columns are available.

questions.stem: After a configuration change, the Constellation portal and Explore Data fail to load for every user. Which two checks are appropriate? (Choose Two)
options: Verify the application settings, alias and authentication types.
Verify the OAuth 2.0 Client Registration rule.
Adjust the number separators in the table UI controls.
Update the class short descriptions.
questions.explanation: When the Constellation portal or Explore Data fails to load, check the application settings, alias and authentication types, and the OAuth 2.0 Client Registration rule. Number separators are a table display issue that is fixed by changing UI controls. Short descriptions affect the object names shown in Explore Data and do not stop pages from loading.

questions.stem: Users browsing Explore Data see a data object listed under an unclear technical name instead of a business-friendly one. What should the developer change?
options: The class short description
The property's reporting optimization
The access token lifetime
The table's UI controls
questions.explanation: Explore Data takes object names from the class short description, so updating it fixes the label. Optimizing a property for reporting fixes missing columns. The access token lifetime fixes repeated login prompts. UI controls fix number separators in tables.
